topic: Shared decision making and patient reported outcomes in rheumatology: HAQ, PROMIS, PROs
synopsis: The 2019 ACR update recommends RA disease-activity measures for regular use. Five measures were selected as preferred: CDAI, DAS28-ESR/CRP, PAS-II, RAPID3, and SDAI. Disease-activity scores are built from combinations of patient-reported measures, provider assessments, laboratory values, and imaging. PAS-II and RAPID3 are patient-report-heavy indices; the Health Assessment Questionnaire sits inside PAS, and RAPID3 contains the Multi-Dimensional HAQ. A parallel functional-status project recommended PROMIS Physical Function 10, MD-HAQ, and HAQ-II. Patient-reported components matter clinically: disease-activity scores that include them are higher in patients with comorbid fibromyalgia. The update tells clinicians who are integrating a measure into the record to select one of the preferred measures, and it does not preclude other measures that meet a minimum standard. This paper does not set out a shared-decision-making procedure, so none is stated here.
